challenge.scenario: A service worker inserts a mention on a customer-service email message.
challenge.finding: Customer conversation privacy may expose external user identity as internal chat mention.
challenge.resolution: Trigger rejects v_message.kind not internal and noninternal thread.

challenge.scenario: A privileged service-role worker inserts a mention with mentioned_by set to a different author than the actual office_messages.author_id stored on the same thread and instance.
challenge.finding: Without a message-author equality verification the service-role caller could impersonate an unrelated support employee in an internal Office chat and create fraudulent notifications or audit references.
challenge.resolution: The canonical BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE mention integrity trigger must query the referenced message by message_id/thread_id/instance_id and reject when v_message.author_id IS DISTINCT FROM new.mentioned_by; verify source and later actual Postgres negative DML.

challenge.scenario: A mention targets employee without access to private chat.
challenge.finding: Private thread existence or metadata could leak across membership boundaries.
challenge.resolution: Trigger calls can_read_office_thread_v1 with mentioned user.

challenge.scenario: A signed-in team member attempts to create a self-mention in an internal_private conversation by submitting their own author UUID as mentioned_user_id through a privileged Office service path.
challenge.finding: If the validator allows self mentions, the system can generate self-notifications and duplicate participant mention state while bypassing the intended recipient-only notification contract.
challenge.resolution: Require private.enforce_office_message_mention_integrity_v1 to reject new.mentioned_user_id=new.mentioned_by and verify thread participant access; add regression text assertion and later native PostgreSQL role negative test.

challenge.scenario: Service worker changes thread_id on existing mention via UPDATE.
challenge.finding: Old valid mention could be retargeted to an unrelated thread without check.
challenge.resolution: BEFORE UPDATE OF identity fields revalidates message/thread/member.

challenge.scenario: Linked order belongs to a different webshop instance.
challenge.finding: Cross-tenant business card can reveal commercial data.
challenge.resolution: private.office_chat_object_exists_v1 checks instance_id and actual target object.

challenge.scenario: Business object card is created by thread reader lacking support permission.
challenge.finding: Content exposes business data beyond roles.

challenge.scenario: An occupied target has legacy invalid link rows.
challenge.finding: New triggers do not clean historical bad rows automatically.
challenge.resolution: Read-only compatibility inventory and manual remediation before target apply.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: Canonical Team Chat 2 Foundation 0065 introduced participant-scoped mentions and business object link tables. Under service_role, direct SQL writes could bypass RPC checks on invalid messages, nonparticipants and cross-tenant object links. Append exact original 20260909204524 Team Chat 2 Integrity before/after triggers in new 0066 after 0065, no prior source mutation. These reject non-internal or cross-instance message/thread references, forged mentioned_by/created_by, unauthorized mentions, and unsupported/mismatched tenant object IDs on INSERT or identity-field UPDATE. Prove full real isolated PG18 68/68 install; actual actor identity and native Supabase still separate. No target writes.
observableOutcomes: Append full byte-identical canonical 0066 Team Chat integrity source with SHA256 header after 0065 and leave all old migrations intact.
New security definer mention integrity trigger checks internal message, valid same-tenant internal thread, authorship and mentioned participant access on INSERT and identity UPDATE.
New object link integrity trigger checks message author, internal thread, creator read+support permission and private tenant-scoped business object existence on INSERT and identity UPDATE.
Both trigger functions direct EXECUTE revoked from public/anon/authenticated; original 0065 RLS and service role table grants preserved.
68 baseline migrations remain source-reviewed; customer tests, TypeScript and complete isolated local PostgreSQL 68/68 clean schema replay and official pre/postflight PASS.
Exact-base bounded 5/5, Edit-Time/Knowledge/Replay PASS, without native Supabase JWT/Storage or final Team Chat owner transfer DONE claim.
unresolvedRisks: Trigger semantics are on selected identity UPDATE fields; nonidentity updates do not revalidate all old metadata; actual integration/actor tests required.
Existing occupied target with invalid mentioned users/business objects would require read-only inventory and remediation before deployment.
Definer function uses caller-supplied author_id and p_actor; forged service_role identity is not blocked by a native session binding, so release still partial.
Local PostgreSQL fixture is not native Supabase security/user ecosystem, provider sends and strict Pro subscription SQL still unmerged.
Next canonical owner transfer migration 20260909204547 is needed to close participant owner lifecycle.
